name: Baker's Mixing
desc: Chaotic advection caught mid-fold — two pigments pulled through an alternating sine flow that stretches and folds them like taffy into razor-thin lamellae, exponentially finer every pass, while elliptic islands of unmixed fluid ride serenely inside the chaos and never blend at all; as pigment lamellae in a dark bath, banded agate strata, a mixing-intensity field that shows only where the fluid is working, sumi ink marbling, or an iridescent oil film.

energy.doc: the Lyapunov exponent — shear per half-step: low leaves a regular flow with fat unmixed islands, high drives global chaos that shreds everything

scale.doc: true optical zoom into the mixing pattern (resolves finer striations, does not enlarge pixels)

speed.doc: stirring rate — how fast the flow alternates between the two shears

density.doc: striation COUNT — how many half-steps of stretching are folded into the frame (mixing age)

sharp.doc: dye edge hardness — soft diffuse gradient through to a hard two-tone partition

hue.doc: hue of the first pigment (the second takes the complement)

x.doc: pan across the flow (the domain is a torus — every position wraps seamlessly)

style.doc: aesthetic: pigment lamellae glowing in a dark bath / matte banded agate strata / abstracted mixing-intensity field where islands go dark / sumi ink on bone paper / iridescent oil film

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the flow phases and the initial dye placement
